notes.title: What's with the different app names on the Store Page?
notes.content:
So "Aam Aadmi" has been released on Steam for everyone, and right away if you load up the Steam page, you will notice that it says "Buy Project Vayu" instead of "Buy Aam Aadmi". Puzzling, you'd think. Maybe it is a scam, or maybe it is something fishy.

Actually, the reason behind this mistake is really stupid, but it is a long story. For those among you who actually know me, you might remember that "Aam Aadmi" is not the only game I am working on. For the past one year, I've been working on an air-combat game. It is a semi-realistic air combat game with somewhat realistic physics and what-not. You know, the usual: somewhat realistic-ish missile system and radar and stealth and etc and etc - at least as far as I can make in a video game. Because the game was set in India and would involve Indian Aircraft, I named it "Project Vayu". 

The thing is, the development time was rather long. It has been one year, and the game is still far from what I would call 'playable'. It is coming along fine, no doubt about that, but it is taking a long time, and the thing with projects this long is that you tend to lose motivation and hope rather quickly, which saps your and energy and will to continue making games. I prefer having fun making the game rather than slogging on and hating every bit of it. I had never published a game on Steam, and waking up every day with the anxiety of whether I will succeed or not is.....annoying, to say the least. 

So, I decided to put aside "Project Vayu" for a while and make a smaller but simpler game to gain confidence and rebuild the passion I have for making video games. I started a new project based on an idea I had noted down long ago, and it all culminated into "Aam Aadmi". I will admit, I spent a lot of time goofing around in the editor playing the game instead of working on it, and I enjoyed every bit of it, even if it increased the development time significantly.

Unfortunately, I had already paid the $100 Steam direct fees and half-filled out the Store page, and since I was short on cash, I had no option but to use the same application I had for "Project Vayu". Even though I changed everything, it seemed the package name doesn't change. This wasn't something I noticed until the game has been released, and by then it was too late. Apparently, there is also no option to change the name as well, so I guess we're stuck with that. 

Project Vayu isn't dead by any means. I still keep working on it when I find the time, and I post video on Youtube when I do. [previewyoutube=hLZLsKrraZo;full][/previewyoutube] 

However, recording gameplay for posting on social media is tedious, and as such I rarely do it. The game is a lot different from what you see here in the video: there are now guided air-to-air munitions and autonomouse air-to-ground munitions with combat-air-teaming capability in the game now, and I haven't posted that now. Plus, there is a work-in-progress detailed SAM system that is also not posted anywhere. If you are interested in seeing how the game turns out, you can go subscribe the youtube channel for updates, and join the discord server as well. 

Cheers,
Mauryan Interactive[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45490372/5d65c8e34dd04d98956dcf308b312df07d7a454d.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45490372/26d44ebccee8fad81a32343d12f9260ad252d992.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: What is "Aam Aadmi" ?
notes.content:
I am happy to announce the release of "Aam Aadmi", a Bollywood action movie-inspired single player FPS. You play as an 'aam aadmi' - a common man living a peaceful life in modern day India - until now. Having his home defiled and his wife kidnapped by corrupt politicians and police officers, he embarks on a journey to dismember the corrupt system without any painkillers. Kick down doors and go guns blazing as you chew through hordes of enemies using a variety of unique, almost-certainly never-seen-before-in-a-video-game guns and of course, your go-to weapon for every occasion - sheer blunt force trauma. 

The inspiration for this game comes from many places. Right off the bat the first thing that comes to mind is the indie FPS "Cop Bastard". I only played the demo, which was rather short, but it was really fun, and showed me how such an idea was not only feasible but also quite fun. 

Cop Bastard wasn't the only inspiration. Similar games inspired by cinema such as "The Hong Kong Massacre", "Trepang2", "Robocop: Rogue City" (this one I haven't played yet, if "Aam Aadmi" does well i might use the revenue earned from it to buy it) and "Maximum Action". Robocop was key, since unlike in the rest of the games I mentioned, you aren't flying around and shooting bad gooners in bullet-time, but are like a force of nature yourself. You don't need cover or concealment, instead you are brazenly ploughing through enemies, kicking things so hard they explode. It is the perfect power-fantasy, I liked the idea the moment I saw it. This is the chief inspiration for the game's core gameplay loop: move slow and hit hard. 

The game is rather short. I built it in a month. I can't help it; the idea struck me all of a sudden when I was at the gym, and now I wanted to play it immediately. Developmental hell is not preferable, and if I can avoid it to make a game I think I would enjoy, then I will. There's no other reason. And despite the many issues in the game, I can safely say that I enjoy playing the game that I have built, and actually wish I had more time and resources to build it even more, were it not for the sake of avoiding the common and deadly mistake of scope creep and letting developmental hell drag on for years instead of month. I'm sure if I did, then by the end of development I would have lost all love for the game along with any motivation for continuing game development. 

That said, I do acknowledge the issues and the bugs, and I am actively working on them. Feedback from players, play testers and friends have allowed me to change and modify the game to a great degree, to the point that the game now looks very different when I look at the older gameplay recordings and screenshots. I am still addressing and fixing new issues as they pop up - as much as I can, at least - and the game will change a lot in the coming days, both in how it looks and plays. 

Cheers,
maskedakshat
